players.product: Helios rack-scale platform (Instinct + EPYC, Infinity Fabric / UALink scale-up)

quarterly_data.signal: AMD's Q2 2026 earnings release says it launched the AMD Helios rackscale solution, which is being deployed by leading AI labs and cloud providers including Anthropic, Cirrascale, HUMAIN, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle, Tensorwave, Vultr and others.

The release's segment table shows Data Center segment operating income of $2,103 million for the three months ended June 27, 2026, versus $1,599 million for the three months ended March 28, 2026 and $(155) million for the three months ended June 28, 2025 (Q2'25 included $800 million in inventory and related charges from the U.S. export control on Instinct MI308). Data Center segment net revenue for the six months ended June 27, 2026 was $12,493 million versus $6,914 million for the six months ended June 28, 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: Data Center segment operating income $2,103 million (three months ended June 27, 2026) vs $1,599 million (March 28, 2026) and $(155) million (June 28, 2025); Data Center six-month net revenue $12,493 million vs $6,914 million

quarterly_data.signal: AMD's Q2 2026 earnings release says that, as part of its expanded collaboration with Microsoft, Azure will add two new AMD EPYC CPU-powered VM series and broaden its deployment of Pensando DPUs to support Azure networking services (the release names no EPYC generation for the VM series). The accompanying Q2 2026 slides say Microsoft and AMD announced an expanded collaboration to deploy AMD Helios and 6th Gen EPYC CPUs at scale across Azure.
quarterly_data.figure: two new AMD EPYC CPU-powered VM series on Microsoft Azure; broader Pensando DPU deployment (no specific figure)
